stem: Which statement about the amygdala and memory is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It is involved in fear and fear memories
options.misconception: None — the amygdala is involved in fear and fear memories.
options.explanation: The amygdala is involved in fear and in fear memories, linking emotional arousal to what is remembered.

options.label: B
options.text: It stores learned motor skills and habits
options.misconception: Assigns procedural memory to the amygdala instead of cerebellum and basal ganglia.
options.explanation: Learned motor skills and habits are procedural memories, which depend mainly on the cerebellum and basal ganglia rather than the amygdala.

options.label: C
options.text: It holds verbal information in working memory
options.misconception: Assigns working memory to the amygdala instead of prefrontal cortex.
options.explanation: Holding verbal information briefly for use is working memory, supported by prefrontal cortex; the amygdala does not maintain it.

options.label: D
options.text: It encodes spatial maps of the surroundings
options.misconception: Assigns hippocampal spatial mapping to the amygdala.
options.explanation: Spatial maps of the surroundings are encoded by hippocampal place cells; the amygdala is tied to fear, not navigation.

options.label: E
options.text: It stores the meanings of words and concepts
options.misconception: Assigns semantic memory storage to the amygdala instead of temporal neocortex.
options.explanation: The meanings of words and concepts are semantic memories stored across the temporal neocortex, not in the amygdala.

context: Learning objective: The amygdala is involved in fear and in fear memories.
